text_blocks.snippet: Residents in Central Illinois should watch out for active phone spoofing, fake municipal invoices, and state text message scams highlighted by the U.S. Attorney's Office For The Central District of Illinois.
snippet_highlighted_words: active phone spoofing, fake municipal invoices, and state text message scams

text_blocks.snippet: Current Scam Trends in Central Illinois

list.snippet: Federal Prosecutor Phone Spoofing: Scammers spoof official phone numbers and pretend to be staff members or attorneys from the U.S. Attorney's Office. They use threats and fear to demand immediate payment or sensitive financial information.

City Department Impersonation: Fraudsters send fake invoices and fraudulent notices using forged city letterhead—often targeting people who recently appeared before local zoning boards like the one in Pekin.

State & Tollway Text Scams: Phishing texts falsely claim your driver’s license is suspended, or that you owe money for delinquent state tolls and traffic fines. These texts include urgent deadlines and fake payment links.
Utility & Provider "Slamming": Deceptive callers pretend to be with local utility or power choice companies to trick residents into switching their electricity or utility providers.
General Fraud & Impersonation: The Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois warns of a rise in family/celebrity impersonation scams, tech support traps, and fake relationship or prize offers.
Do not pay over the phone: Government agencies, courts, and utility companies will never demand immediate cash, gift cards, or wire transfers over the phone.
Verify independently: Hang up immediately. Look up the official phone number of the agency or business yourself, and call them directly to check the claim.
Review financial alerts: Financial institutions like the Central Illinois Credit Union advise never clicking unsolicited links in text messages or emails.
Call the Illinois Attorney General’s Scam Hotline at 1-800-243-0618.
Forward suspicious state text messages to scamalert@ils.gov (or report to local police dispatch).
